compiled_state.description:
Six subsystem agents triaged every substantial comment in `src/rebar` (439 files) against the
maintainer's destination taxonomy: history belongs in tickets, architecture in ADRs, logic in code,
contracts in schema, and comments carry only proximate just-in-time context in concise language.

Total recoverable: **~2,033 lines**. Per shard: reconciler ~970, plan_review+workflow ~230,
store/reducer ~230, llm core ~218, commands/CLI ~205, root/services ~180.

The largest single category is self-referential: **prose explaining the 800-LOC cap**, occupying the
budget it describes. 28 sites in the reconciler alone carry variants of "RELOCATED VERBATIM out of
transport.py; this module changes no behaviour. The move is forced by the LOCKED 800-line cap." The
loop closes at `outbound_differ.py:164`, which records that a fix had to "buy its lines back from
real duplication instead of from comments" because the module sat at the cap.

Headroom recovered where it is tightest: `runner.py` 3 → ~48 lines (the repo's #1 hotspot, 88
commits, whose 371-line method sits at its C901 ceiling); `_ref_lock.py` 1 → ~21; `dispatch_one.py`
14 → ~57; `inbound_differ.py` 18 → ~66; `fetcher.py` 29 → ~80.

Honest counterweight, and it must not be lost: **comment triage cannot fix three files.**
`_store/event_append.py` (791) recovers ~10 lines; `reducer/_processors.py` (777) recovers ~3;
`signing.py` (798) recovers ~5-8. Their comments ARE the replay-compat and security invariants. Each
shard identified the real call-graph seam instead, and those splits are out of scope here.

Every shard produced a `do_not_move` list — blocks that look relocatable but are load-bearing. Those
lists are the protection record and must be preserved (appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md`) so a
future sweep does not re-flag them. Examples: "on DC 8.17.1 the `fields.parent` write answers HTTP
204 and is silently ignored. Do not 'simplify' that extra round trip away"; "ACLI's `--out`/`--in`
are INVERTED relative to the naive reading"; "READ FROM `exc.response.headers`, NOT `exc.headers`".

Verified-stale comments found along the way (correctness, not verbosity): six sites say the
deterministic floor is "P1-P9" while `DET_CHECKS` has 11 entries and runs P1..P11; three sites in
`llm/` assert an Anthropic constraint that `structured.py:228-238` explicitly calls "a stale
rationale" and "a relic" 210 lines below one of them; `_backend_registry.py:3` says "STUB:
signatures pinned, bodies to be implemented" while `select_backend` is imported by 13 modules;
`_io/__init__.py:14` says the import side "lands in a later sub-task" six lines above the line that
imports it; `reducer/llm_format.py:1-28` documents a key map that omits four keys present directly
below it and cites a module path that does not exist.

~13 new ADRs are proposed across the shards, each consolidating an argument currently restated 4-8
times. The largest: "one idempotent transform, applied fit-then-normalize, on the local side only" —
the same four-paragraph argument at 8 sites, warning that "Swapping the two re-introduces a diff
that never converges."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All six shards complete, each landing separately
- [ ] Each shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` before that shard's edits land
- [ ] History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first
- [ ] Proposed ADRs are written and the inline blocks reduced to citations
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected, not deleted, where they document a live invariant
- [ ] No file's comment density is reduced by deleting a load-bearing invariant

## CORRECTION (plan-review BLOCK, criteria E1/E2/F1)

Two ACs were unmeasurable: the ~2,033-line recovery headline had no covering criterion, and
"Proposed ADRs are written" named no specific ADR set. Superseded below. The line-recovery
criterion is deliberately framed as a MEASURED-AND-RECORDED outcome, not a fixed target — this
is the same correction the 9ce8 shard's own plan-review already blessed ("the number is an
output of the work, not an input to it"); mandating a fixed >=2,000-line floor would contradict
that and incentivise manufactured relocations.

## Disposition vocabulary (what the ACs measure against)

A **unit** is one contiguous comment block (a run of adjacent comment lines, or a single
docstring). Every in-scope unit gets exactly one disposition:

- **RELOCATE** (non-KEEP) — the prose moves to its taxonomy destination (history -> ticket,
  architecture -> ADR, contract -> schema) and the inline block is reduced to a one-line
  citation. Recovered lines = block minus citation.
- **DELETE** (non-KEEP) — redundant/obsolete prose with no destination worth keeping; removed
  outright. Recovered lines = whole block. Only after confirming it is not load-bearing.
- **KEEP** (KEEP-class) — proximate just-in-time context that belongs exactly where it is;
  untouched, not counted as recovered.
- **DO_NOT_MOVE** (KEEP-class) — looks relocatable but is load-bearing (measured external-API
  fact, anti-refactor warning, or a lint/type-checker pragma); retained VERBATIM and recorded on
  the shard's `do_not_move` list. Not counted as recovered.
- **CORRECT-IN-PLACE** (KEEP-class) — a verified-stale comment documenting a LIVE invariant;
  the text is corrected where it sits, not moved. Not counted as recovered.

"non-KEEP unit" in the ACs = the RELOCATE and DELETE classes only. KEEP, DO_NOT_MOVE and
CORRECT-IN-PLACE are KEEP-class: retained (corrected in place where stale) and never counted as
recovered lines. Completeness is verified by confirming every in-scope unit carries exactly one
of these five labels.

## Acceptance Criteria (supersedes the list above)

- [ ] All six shards complete, each landing as a separate stacked change in the dependency order
      9ce8 -> 4fc1 -> 4b94 -> ad16 -> da4c -> ab77.
- [ ] Each shard MEASURES and RECORDS on its own ticket the actual comment lines it recovered (by
      diff line-count), and this parent records the net total across shards. Per the 9ce8
      correction the ~2,033 / per-shard figures are OUTPUTS to be measured, NOT targets: no
      relocation is manufactured to reach an estimate, and a shard recovering fewer lines than
      estimated is not a failure provided every non-KEEP unit in scope was correctly
      dispositioned.
- [ ] Every ADR enumerated in the shard tickets (the new ADRs and the amendments to ADR
      0028/0055/0031/0035) EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is
      collapsed -- destination first, then the relocation. This AC is met per-shard against that
      shard's own enumerated ADR set.
- [ ] History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a
      ticket filed first.
- [ ] Each shard's `do_not_move` list is appended to `.joe-janitor/tools.md` before that shard's
      edits land.
- [ ] Verified-stale comments are corrected where they document a live invariant, deleted only
      where obsolete.
- [ ] No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings
      stay verbatim.
- [ ] No behaviour change: the full test suite AND `make lint` / `make typecheck` pass
      unchanged across every shard. Inline pragma comments (`# noqa`, `# type: ignore`,
      `# ruff:`, `# tickets-boundary-ok`) and any docstring a test reads via introspection
      are load-bearing by definition and go on every shard's `do_not_move` list -- they are
      never treated as relocatable prose.
compiled_state.title: Comment triage: relocate history, rationale and contracts out of src
